title: Hello
description: The first frame on the connection, in BOTH directions — one type name, two shapes, told apart by who received it. The plugin's carries the token and is refused without it; the companion's answers. A frame of any other type before hello closes the connection with hello_required.

v.description: Protocol version. A shape change is a new version, never an edit of v1 in place.

harness.description: The harness this plugin translates for, e.g. hermes.

token.description: 🔴 SECRET-CLASS. Read from $UFFICI_HOME/wire-token, compared in constant time, and NEVER logged by either side — not at any level, not in an error, not inside a whole-frame dump.

contextBudgetTokens.description: The harness's share of its window for platform content. The platform sizes to it with its own estimator; the companion never estimates.

processId.description: Optional. A nonce the plugin mints once per harness PROCESS and sends on every hello. The same id on a reconnect is the same process, still working on what it acknowledged; a different id is a restarted harness that holds nothing of the old one's turns, so the companion delivers what the old process had acknowledged again. Not a secret, and not an identity: a new one per process start. An older plugin that omits it keeps the old rule — acknowledged requests are never redelivered.

drift.description: Optional. What in the harness's own configuration reaches past Uffici, as the plugin read it at this hello — a client-reported signal (#1958 decision 27), shown by `uffici doctor` and NEVER a refusal: no value here closes a connection, holds a ring or fails a setup step. Each kind is the plugin's reading of one source; a kind the plugin could not read is ABSENT, an empty list means it read none. An older plugin omits the whole object, which the doctor reports as not reported. Names only — never a URL, a header, a path or a credential; the plugin clips each name to the bound and the list to its length rather than ever sending a frame the companion would refuse. An unknown kind is ignored.

mcpServers.description: The names of the MCP servers the harness has configured and enabled besides Uffici's own tools: tools whose calls never pass through the platform.

channels.description: The harness's other live channels — platforms enabled and configured besides Uffici, on which this agent also answers outside the platform.

localMemory.description: The harness's settings that keep a memory of its own beside Uffici's, by key (for Hermes: `memory.memory_enabled`, `memory.user_profile_enabled` still on, or `memory.provider` naming another provider).

harnessSupport.description: Optional. The harness versions this plugin release supports, and the plugin's verdict on `harnessVersion` against them, as it read them at this hello (#2414) — a client-reported signal shown by `uffici doctor` and NEVER a refusal: no well-formed value here closes a connection (a `range` past its bound is malformed like any other field, which is why the plugin holds its range under it), holds a ring or fails a setup step. The plugin owns the range because only it knows the interfaces it was written against and how its harness numbers releases; the companion never parses a harness version. An older plugin omits the whole object, which the doctor reports as not reported.

range.description: The supported versions in the plugin's own words, e.g. `>=0.21.5,<0.22`.

supported.description: Whether `harnessVersion` is inside `range`. ABSENT when the plugin could not read the harness's version — the doctor then says so rather than guessing either way.

agentSlug.description: Known from wave 1b; the fixture supplies a fixed value.

features.description: Optional. What this companion can carry beyond the frames every v1 companion does, so a newer plugin never sends an older companion a field it would drop. `question`: a post may carry a question, which reaches the person as the question card. `redelivery`: a harness process that restarts is handed again every request its predecessor had accepted, so a plugin leaves an interrupted turn to the companion rather than resuming it itself. `tools`: the plugin may call `tools.list` and `tools.call`, and a post may carry `citations` and `activity`. An absent list means none; a name the plugin does not know is ignored.
